prompt:
The block is being balanced this week, so the commissioning engineer shoots the whole riser up the stairwell before the next round of adjustment.

One riser feeds a cast iron radiator group on each of four landings of an old block. On every group's return pipe there is a balancing valve with the turns engraved round its cap, and beside it a five cell temperature strip with a number printed in each cell: 45, 50, 55, 60 and 65. The commissioning sheet taped to the wall by the ground floor group gives the flow temperature as 70 and the setting made at each landing: ground floor 1.0 turns, first floor 2.0, second floor 2.5, top floor 4.0. The wider a valve is opened, the more of the riser's water that group takes.

What each strip shows at its own return is what the commissioning sheet does not give.
easy_question: Does this picture show a heating riser up a stairwell with a radiator group on each landing? Answer yes or no only.

steps.ask: Read the temperature strip beside the ground floor group and the one beside the top floor group, each printed with its own row of numbers. Answer with one of: the darkened cell on the top floor strip carries the larger number of the two; the darkened cell on the ground floor strip carries the larger number of the two; the same printed number is darkened on both strips.

Look at the temperature strips on all four landings and at which cell has darkened on each. Answer with one of: each of the four strips has a different cell darkened; all four strips have the same cell darkened; two of the strips have the same cell darkened and the other two are different.
